1.w: My brothers, do not in partiality hold the faith from our Lord Jesus Christ of glory.

2.w: For if a man might come into your⁺ synagogue in splendid apparel with a gold ring, and a poor one in filthy apparel also might come in,

3.w: and you⁺ might look upon the [man] bearing the splendid apparel and might say, “You sit here well,” and to the poor one might say, “You stand,” or, “Sit there under my footstool,”

4.w: then did you⁺ not make a distinction among yourselves and become judges [with] evil reasonings?

5.w: Listen, my beloved brothers: Did not God choose the poor in this world [to be] rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that He promised to those loving Him?

6.w: But you⁺ dishonored the poor one. Do not the rich oppress you⁺, and they drag you⁺ into court?

7.w: Do they not blaspheme the good Name having been called upon you⁺?

8.w: If indeed you⁺ fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you⁺ are doing well.

9.w: But if you⁺ show partiality, you⁺ are working sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

10.w: For whoever shall keep the whole law, but shall stumble in one [part], he has become guilty of all.

11.w: For the One having said, “You shall not commit adultery,” also said, “You shall not murder.” But if you do not commit adultery, but you do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.

12.w: So speak and so act as being about to be judged by the law of freedom.

13.w: For judgment without mercy [will be] to the one not having done mercy. Mercy exults over judgment.

14.w: What [is] the gain, my brothers, if anyone says to have faith, but has no works? Is the faith able to save him?

15.w: Now if a brother or a sister is naked and lacking of daily food,

16.w: and anyone of you⁺ says to them, “Go in peace; be warmed and be filled,” but does not give to them the needful things for the body, what [is] the gain?

17.w: So also, faith, if it has no works, is dead by itself.

18.w: But someone will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show to me your faith without works, and I will show to you faith by my works.

19.w: You believe that God is one. You do well! Even the demons believe [that], and shudder!

20.w: But do you want to know, O foolish man, that faith without works is idle?

21.w: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, having offered his son Isaac upon the altar?

22.w: You see that faith was working with his works, and by works, faith was perfected.

23.w: And the Scripture was fulfilled, the one saying, “And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.

24.w: You⁺ see that a man is justified by works and not by faith alone.

25.w: And likewise was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works, having received the messengers and having sent [them] out by another way?

26.w: For just as the body without spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
